title: Staged Cohort Activation: Gateways, Rollbacks, and Measurement for Q2 Private Deployments
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Goal: Define and approve a quarterly playbook for staged cohort activations of Private/VPC/on-prem enterprise customers that standardizes gateway configuration, acceptance gates, rollback criteria, observability signals, and executive reporting requirements. This ticket scopes the product-level runbook, activation matrix (cohort sizes, cadence, eligibility), cross-functional owners, and measurement plan for Q2 activations.

Background: Sales and Customer Success have increased commitment velocity for isolated instances. To avoid ad-hoc work and operational risk, we need a repeatable activation pattern that balances time-to-value with safety. Current pilot runs (Jan–Feb) surfaced inconsistent gateway setup steps, unclear latency budgets, and missing tracer-level observability for on-prem networking issues.

Deliverables:
- Activation playbook document (step-by-step) for staged rollouts including preflight checklist, canary cohort sizes, and cutover tasks.
- Standardized gateway templates (VPC peering, NAT, port mappings) and template validation checks.
- Acceptance & rollback gates tied to clear SLO/health signals (p95 token latency, error rates, degraded-model fallback success).
- Activation matrix: recommended cohort sizes and pacing for small/medium/large enterprise tenants.
- Measurement dashboard definition and default alert thresholds for operations and CS.
- Post-activation remediation checklist and customer-facing release notes template.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Playbook written, reviewed by Eng, Security, and Support, and stored in Confluence.
2) Template gateway configurations committed to repo and validated by infra team in a staging environment.
3) Dashboard and alerts created in Ops dashboard (first pass) with signals: p95 latency, 5xx rate per minute, token-cost delta >10%, KV cache hitrate below runbook threshold, and N+1 health probe failures.
4) Canary run executed with an internal lighthouse customer or a synthetic tenant; runbook used end-to-end and results documented.
5) Rollback procedure executed in staging and verified to restore previous capacity within allowable RTO.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- We will support two activation lanes for Q2: 'fast' for small greenfield tenants (<=3 GPUs, low customization) and 'controlled' for large/customized on-prem installs. Supporting more lanes increases complexity of templates and testing matrices.
- Security review will be scoped to ensure no customer-sensitive configs are leaked; full HSM/KMS integration will be out of scope for the first wave.
- Observability instrumentation requires small runtime agent additions that may add up to 1–2% CPU overhead; we will gate rollout on infra sign-off.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Network misconfiguration causing higher-than-acceptable latency. Mitigation: automated validation step + traffic shaping tests in staging.
- Risk: Inadequate rollback testing. Mitigation: mandatory rollback rehearsals during the canary run.
- Risk: Customer confusion over activation windows. Mitigation: CS will get a templated activation calendar and pre-activation checklist.

Who needs to review / sign off: Eng Prod Lead (Liam Chen), SRE Lead (Maya Patel), Security (Omar Diaz), Customer Success Lead (Priya Singh), VP Product (Eleanor Brooks).

Next steps (owner tags):
- Product (Aisha): finalize playbook draft and circulate for review (due 2025-01-24).
- Infra (Eng owner): create gateway templates and validation scripts (due 2025-02-07).
- SRE: define dashboard panels and alert rules (due 2025-02-14).
- CS: identify lighthouse customer for canary (due 2025-02-10).
- Security: quick-scan of templates (due 2025-02-12).

Notes on measurement: Primary KPIs for the initiative will be time-to-activation (days from contract signature to first successful routing), incidence rate within 14 days (number of incidents per activation), and 30-day customer satisfaction score post-activation. Secondary KPIs include per-tenant token cost variance and average KV cache hit rate.

Longer-term: If playbook proves repeatable, we will fold activation templates into the Console onboarding flows and add automated preflight validation to Redwood Private installer.
